subject: maths
chapterTitle: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
title: Solving by substitution

goals: Solve a pair of equations by substitution
Check your answer in both equations

cards.title: The idea
cards.body: Make one variable the subject of one equation, then put that expression into the other equation. You're left with one equation in one variable, which you can solve.

rows.value: From one equation, write y in terms of x (or x in terms of y)
Substitute it into the other equation
Solve for the one variable left
Put that value back to find the other

cards.question: From x + y = 7, what is y in terms of x?
cards.why: Move x to the other side: y = 7 − x.

cards.question: Solve x + y = 7 and x − y = 1 by substitution.
Solving x = 2y and x + y = 9, what is y?
cards.why: Substitute x = 2y into x + y = 9: 2y + y = 9, so 3y = 9 and y = 3. Then x = 6.

cards.title: Pick the easy variable
cards.body: Choose the variable with a coefficient of 1 or −1 to make the subject. It avoids fractions and keeps the working short.
cards.remember: Always check your answer in both original equations.

cards.question: For 3x + y = 10 and 2x − 5y = 1, which is the easiest first step?
cards.why: y has a coefficient of 1 in the first equation, so y = 10 − 3x needs no fractions.

points: Make one variable the subject, substitute, solve, then back-substitute
Pick a variable with coefficient 1 or −1
